title: “And craving, previously unknowing — which is of sensual desire, of defilement — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a…
content: “And craving, previously unknowing — which is of sensual desire, of defilement — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to arise again in the future. And anger, previously unknowing — which is of ill-will, of fault — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to arise again in the future. And ignorance, previously unknowing — which is of delusion, of fault — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to arise again in the future. Therefore, a monk thus attained has attained the supreme peace of the peaceful state. Monks, this is the supreme noble peace — namely, the peace of greed, hatred, and delusion.”

title: “Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful…
content: “Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is a samana.”

title: “Bound with sinews and bones, Plastered with flesh and skin, This body is covered by skin — Truth is not seen as it is. Within,…
content:
“Bound with sinews and bones,
Plastered with flesh and skin,
This body is covered by skin —
Truth is not seen as it is.

Within, it is full of liver, bladder,
Heart, lungs,
Kidneys and spleen,
Nasal mucus, saliva, sweat, fat,
Blood, synovial fluid, bile, and lymph.

From these nine streams,
Impurity constantly flows —
From the eyes, discharge flows,
From the ears, discharge flows.

From the nostrils, mucus flows,
From the mouth, sometimes vomit —
Bile and phlegm flow —
From the body, sweat and dirt.

In the hollow of the head,
The brain is full.
The fool, led by ignorance,
Thinks it is beautiful.

When it lies dead, swollen,
Livid, discarded in a charnel ground,
Relatives no longer care.

Dogs, jackals, wolves, worms,
Crows, vultures, and other creatures eat it.”

title: “He who dwells attending to the beautiful, Unrestrained in the senses, Immoderate in food, Lazy, inactive — Māra overthrows him As wind a weak tree.”…
content:
“He who dwells attending to the beautiful,
Unrestrained in the senses,
Immoderate in food,
Lazy, inactive —
Māra overthrows him
As wind a weak tree.”

“He who dwells contemplating the foul,
Well-restrained in the senses,
Moderate in food,
Faithful, energetic —
Māra does not overthrow him,
As wind a rocky mountain.”

title: Elder Nun Sumedhā: Remember this human body — Compared to a water bubble — Full of misfortunes, Empty, without core — See the aggregates as…
content:
Elder Nun Sumedhā:

Remember this human body —
Compared to a water bubble —
Full of misfortunes,
Empty, without core —
See the aggregates as impermanent!
Remember the many dangers of hell.

Remember the great charnel ground —
Because of continuous rebirth —
Because of fear of crocodiles —
Remember the Four Noble Truths.

The deathless water is here —
Why would one drink a hundred bitters?
All sensual pleasures
Are truly a hundred thousand bitter.

The deathless water is here!
Why would one delight in feverish sensual pleasures?
All sensual pleasures burn,
Seething and blistering.

There are no enemies here!
Why delight in hostile sensual pleasures?
The king of fire, thieves, water, enemies —
Common enemies are many.

Here there is liberation!
Why let sensual pleasures kill and bind?
In sensual pleasures there is killing and binding —
Delighting in sensual pleasures brings much suffering.

A blazing grass torch —
If you hold it and don’t let go, you’ll be burned.
Sensual pleasures are like a torch —
They burn anyone who doesn’t escape.

Do not accept small sensual pleasures,
Abandoning great, expansive happiness.
Do not be like a fish swallowing a hook,
Then later suffering calamity.

Subdue sensual desire within sensual desires,
Like a dog tied with a leash.
Do not let sensual desires devour you,
Like a hungry man devouring a dog.

Suffering is truly boundless,
It causes much mental distress.
You are tied to sensual desires —
Abandon impermanent sensual desires.

Here, there is no aging!
Why pursue sensual desires that age?
Every birth, everywhere,
Is subject to disease and death —

Here there is no aging, no death —
This is the path without aging,
Without death, without sorrow,
Without enemies, without bonds,
Without stumbling, without fear,
Without burning, without falling.

This goal, many have attained —
This goal is the deathless.
Now it should be realized.
If one is rightly attentive,
Without exertion,
One cannot realize it.

This is the cause, the source —
This is the very root —
Endure the Teacher’s word!
This is the first link —
That is Nibbāna —
If we love the Dhamma.

Thus, with faith,
They spoke these excellent words,
Words full of wisdom —
Supreme, ultimate —
They are disgusted with renewed existence —
Through disgust, craving ceases.

title: “That is so, great king. That is so, great king. All beings are subject to death, end in death, and do not escape death. Just…
content:
“That is so, great king. That is so, great king. All beings are subject to death, end in death, and do not escape death. Just as, great king, all the pots made by a potter, whether unfired or fired, are subject to breakage, end in breakage, and do not escape breakage — so too, great king, all beings are subject to death, end in death, and do not escape death.

All beings will die,
Life ends with death,
According to their kamma they go,
Reaping fruits of good and evil —
Evil kamma leads to hell,
Good kamma to heaven.
Therefore do good,
Accumulate for the future life,
Merits for the future life
Are a support for beings.”

title: “Craving, monks, is a net that widens the wandering, it sticks; because of this craving, this world is destroyed, bound, tangled like a ball of…
content: “Craving, monks, is a net that widens the wandering, it sticks; because of this craving, this world is destroyed, bound, tangled like a ball of thread, like a tangled skein, like muñja grass and babaja reeds, unable to pass beyond the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower realm, saṃsāra.”

title: “Suppose, monks, a man is struck by a single arrow. They do not strike him with a second arrow. Thus, monks, that man experiences the…
content: “Suppose, monks, a man is struck by a single arrow. They do not strike him with a second arrow. Thus, monks, that man experiences the feeling of one arrow. So too, monks, a well-taught noble disciple, when touched by a painful feeling, does not sorrow, grieve, lament, beat his breast, or become distraught. He experiences one feeling — a bodily feeling, not a mental feeling. Touched by that painful feeling, he does not feel aversion. Because he does not feel aversion toward that painful feeling, the underlying tendency to aversion toward painful feeling does not persist. Touched by that painful feeling, he does not delight in sensual pleasures. Why? Because, monks, the well-taught noble disciple knows an escape from painful feeling other than sensual pleasure. Not delighting in sensual pleasure, the underlying tendency to greed for pleasant feeling does not persist. He knows as it actually is the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape regarding these feelings. Because he knows … the underlying tendency to ignorance regarding neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling does not persist. If he feels a pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is not bound. If he feels a painful feeling, he feels it as one who is not bound. If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is not bound. This, monks, is called a well-taught noble disciple who is not bound by birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is not bound by suffering.”

title: “Monks, form is impermanent, both in the past and in the future, not to mention the present. Seeing this, monks, a well-taught noble disciple has…
content: “Monks, form is impermanent, both in the past and in the future, not to mention the present. Seeing this, monks, a well-taught noble disciple has no regret for past form, does not delight in future form, and practices disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation regarding present form. Feeling is impermanent … Perception is impermanent … Formations are impermanent … Consciousness is impermanent, both in the past and in the future, not to mention the present. Seeing this, monks, a well-taught noble disciple has no regret for past consciousness, does not delight in future consciousness, and practices disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation regarding present consciousness.”

title: “And what, monks, is non-restraint? Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a…
content: “And what, monks, is non-restraint? Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms, praises them, and dwells with lust for them, then that monk, monks, should understand: ‘I have fallen away from wholesome states.’ The Tathāgata calls this ‘falling away.’ … There are sounds cognizable by the ear … odors … tastes … touches … There are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk delights in those phenomena, praises them, and dwells with lust for them, then that monk should understand: ‘I have fallen away from wholesome states.’ The Tathāgata calls this ‘falling away.’ Thus, monks, is non-restraint.”
